rationale: This is a mechanical union of two already-tested archive signals (TotalPhysicalCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion and NetHardAssetCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion) whose legs are near-identical in construction, so it is a cosmetic consolidation unlikely to teach anything new about the mechanism beyond which of the two parents dominates.

Swapping the R&D-intensity gate for a knowledge-stock-share gate is a defensible attempt to distinguish stock composition from spending intensity, though the two gates are likely highly correlated so the discriminating power of the test may be modest.

Preserving the sign of the allocation contrast before weighting by the endowment converts a one-sided cohort screen into a genuine two-sided interaction, which is a substantive functional-form test with an internally consistent positive expected sign.

The three-year lag on the research gate is an economically motivated and genuinely new twist (harvest cohort rather than spending cohort), but changing the rent leg to gross profit per asset at the same time confounds attribution and edges toward the published gross-profitability channel.

Because the leg is a within-firm TS_RANK, adding a smooth, slow-moving R&D stock to the denominator will barely reorder the firm's own history — and for the many firms with no reported R&D the expression is literally unchanged — making this a near-null cosmetic variant of an archived signal.

The second leg is degenerate for non-R&D firms: coalescing xrd to zero before IND_ADJ makes their own-history rank track the negative of the industry R&D mean rather than any firm attribute, so a large fraction of the sample is sorted on an industry time trend, and the stated "full coverage" claim obscures this artifact.
